2026-11-17.title: Tuesday of the Thirty-third Week in Ordinary Time · St Elizabeth of Hungary, Religious
readings: I stand at the door and knock
I will seat the victor beside me on my throne
Today salvation has come to this house
2026-11-17.alt: Memorial of St Elizabeth of Hungary.
2026-11-17.verse: For the Son of Man came to seek out and to save the lost.
theo: To the church of Laodicea, rich and comfortable, Christ speaks his sharpest words: “you are neither cold nor hot… because you are lukewarm… I am about to spit you out of my mouth.” Then, immediately, the tenderest: “Listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you, and you with me.” Christ does not break doors; he knocks.

Zacchaeus is a chief tax collector, rich and despised. He climbs a sycamore just to see Jesus. Jesus stops, looks up, and calls him by name: “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down; for I must stay at your house today.” Grace comes first; conversion follows. Zacchaeus gives half his goods to the poor and repays fourfold. St Elizabeth of Hungary, a queen who spent her wealth on the sick and poor and died at twenty-four, shows the same transformation: when Christ comes in, the purse opens.
outline: Ask: is there a door in your life you keep closed to Jesus?
He waits for us to open.
Point 3 · Salvation comes to the house
“Today salvation has come to this house.”
live: Invite Jesus into one area you keep from him.
Repair one injustice or debt this week.
2026-11-17.prayer: Lord Jesus, you stand at the door and knock. Let me hear your voice and open, rescue me from lukewarmness, and like Zacchaeus and St Elizabeth, let my heart and hands open to the poor. Amen.

quick: Christ knocks; he does not break the door.
When Jesus comes in, generosity follows.
2026-11-17.action: Repair one injustice or debt this week.
2026-11-17.question: Which door am I keeping closed to Christ?

homily: Dear friends, to the church of Laodicea, rich and comfortable, Christ speaks his sharpest words: because you are lukewarm, neither cold nor hot, I am about to spit you out of my mouth (Revelation 3:16). Comfort can make a Christian lukewarm without his noticing.

But immediately follow the tenderest words in the book: I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in and eat with you, and you with me (Revelation 3:20). Christ does not break doors. He knocks, and waits.

Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector and rich, wanted to see Jesus, and because he was short he climbed a sycamore tree. Jesus stopped, looked up and said: Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today. And salvation came to that house as Zacchaeus gave half his goods to the poor (Luke 19:5–9).

Today we remember St Elizabeth of Hungary, a young princess who opened the door of her heart and her treasury to the poor. Where is Christ knocking in your life today? Open the door: one generous gift, one visit, one reconciliation. Amen.
kids: Children, Zacchaeus climbed a tree to see Jesus, and Jesus came to his house! Open your heart to Jesus today by sharing with someone in need.

intro: Theme: “I stand at the door and knock.”
Christ knocks, warns against lukewarmness, and brings salvation to the house that opens.

sub: He does not force the door.
He wants to share a meal with us.
q: I slept, but my heart was awake. Listen! my beloved is knocking. “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one.”
Listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you, and you with me.
points.apply: Open one closed area of your life to Christ.

q: You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.
I know your works; you are neither cold nor hot. I wish that you were either cold or hot. So, because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I am about to spit you out of my mouth.
points.apply: Choose one fervent act of love for God today.

q: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak.
Then Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham. For the Son of Man came to seek out and to save the lost.”

concl: Open the door; Christ is knocking.
Let your conversion reach your wallet.
2026-11-17.resolve: Give generously to the poor this week, as Elizabeth did.
